title: exists_reducedConstantLowerShriekReductionData
statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], f:X → Spec k a separated finite-type curve of dimension at most one [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting], X reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme], j:U → X an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], and r a prime. Put R=ULift(Z/rZ) and let R_U/(r) denote the constant R-module sheaf with value R/(r) [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. There exist a scheme Y, a finite surjective morphism ν:Y → X [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism], a dense open V of X, a scheme U′, morphisms j′:U′ → Y and ν′:U′ → U, such that ν followed by f is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], ν restricted over V is an isomorphism, j′ is an open immersion, the square (j′,ν′,ν,j) is cartesian [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and j′_! R_U′/(r) [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] satisfies the eight assertions for Y → Spec k [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions]. Equivalently, ReducedConstantLowerShriekReductionData(f,j,r) [k1-reduced-constant-lower-shriek-reduction-data] holds.

proof.text: Install the structure morphism f as X.Over Spec k and apply exists_finite_smooth_modification_of_reduced_curve. Install the separated, locally finite type, quasi-compact and smooth witnesses, and combine the dimension witness with them to obtain IsCurve (ν ≫ f).

The restriction ν over the dense open V is an isomorphism, hence its underlying map is surjective. Therefore V is contained in the range of ν, by morphismRestrict_base_coe. Since ν is finite its range is closed. A closed set containing a dense set is the whole space, so ν is surjective. This is the Lean proof hsurj, using ν.isClosedMap.isClosed_range and Dense.mono. Form the standard pullback U′ = Y ×_X U; its first projection is an open immersion by base change, and IsPullback.of_hasPullback gives the cartesian square.

For every smooth curve g over k, split on whether r casts to zero in k. If it does, CharP.charP_iff_prime_eq_zero installs CharP k r and assertions_constantModSheaf_of_charP gives the constant-coefficient assertions. Otherwise use assertions_constantModSheaf_of_ne_zero. The coefficient quotient is finite because ULift (ZMod r) is finite. Both existing assertion declarations reside in SmoothCalculations, retaining the thm-sc-main curve-calculation route and including disconnected, empty and zero-dimensional smooth sources.

Apply smoothConstantLowerShriekAssertions_of_constant to this family of constant-coefficient assertions, the smooth curve ν ≫ f, and the pullback immersion j′. Package the geometric witnesses, their properties, the cartesian square and the resulting assertions into ReducedConstantLowerShriekReductionData.

proof_origin: Stacks 0A3Q normalization paragraph; surjectivity follows from closed range and dense isomorphism locus. Existing Kummer and Artin--Schreier assertions on all smooth curves followed by the localization assembly of Stacks 03SG. Lean reduction written by U2.
